# Aman Gupta

> Aman Gupta is a Principal Machine Learning Engineer at Nubank, working on LLM training and alignment, efficient inference, and the evaluation of large-scale AI agents.

I build and study foundation models and AI agents that operate reliably at scale — research that survives contact with production.

I lead company-wide research on AI agents, foundation models, and LLMs at Nubank, where the systems we build serve more than 135 million customers. My work sits at the intersection of large-scale optimization, deep learning, and language models.

Before Nubank I spent six years at LinkedIn, most recently as a Senior Staff Machine Learning Engineer and Senior Manager in Core AI, where I led the team compressing and distilling LinkedIn's ranking foundation model and drove large-scale optimization across Feed, Ads, and Jobs. Earlier I was a Senior Machine Learning Research Scientist at Apple and a software engineer at Amazon. I studied at Carnegie Mellon and BITS Pilani.

## Research threads

### Agents in production

Getting agents past a demo means being able to say, with evidence, that they will behave on the next hundred million conversations. I work on evaluation harnesses rigorous enough to gate a deployment, and on the failure modes that only appear once real customers are on the other end.

- [KDD 2026] Building Customer Support AI Agents at 100M-User Scale: An Evaluation-Driven Framework (KDD 2026). https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08867
- [Tutorial] Building Production LLM Agents: An Evaluation-Driven Playbook (CIKM 2026, half-day tutorial · Nov 2026).
- [Talk] SimulationMaxxing: How we ship agents 20× faster (AI Engineer, with Shreya Rajpal · Jul 2026). https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KMR_RBoCa4M

### Alignment and post-training

Preference optimization is usually studied through its objective, but the shape of the reward and the robustness of the reward model matter just as much. I look at where the standard recipes are brittle and what to change so alignment holds up outside the benchmark.

- [ICML 2025] AlphaPO: Reward Shape Matters for LLM Alignment (ICML 2025). https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.03884
- [ICML 2025] On the Robustness of Reward Models for Language Model Alignment (ICML 2025). https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.07271

### Efficiency at scale

A model that cannot be served is a result, not a product. This thread covers compressing and distilling large models down to a serving budget, quantizing optimizer state so training fits, and scheduling inference so latency targets survive real traffic.

- [EMNLP 2025] Scaling Down, Serving Fast: Compressing and Deploying Efficient LLMs for Recommendation Systems (EMNLP 2025). https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14305
- [arXiv 2025] Effective Quantization of Muon Optimizer States (arXiv 2025). https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.23106
- [NeurIPS 2025] LLM Query Scheduling with Prefix Reuse and Latency Constraints (NeurIPS 2025). https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.04677
